It gates

Actors take one too, with

Positions themselves are still yours to keep. The engine knows the answer to “can he touch it”; it does not know where in the room either of them is standing, so a room-listing paragraph that changes with the player’s square is still a
rule you write.
Possession is a different question again, and

answers it: is this thing anywhere under them — in their hands, or in a bag on their belt, to any depth? It is true in the dark, in another room, and offstage, because owning a thing has nothing to do with seeing it.

inlineContent.text: It gates no movement and opens nothing. It exists so that a door leading nowhere is still a door to any verb that asks.
A door is also a way through
by name
, not only by direction.
and
all take the exit the door gates, from either side — the engine finds the door on the current room’s exits and makes the same move
would, so a shut door refuses in the same words, a locked one reads as shut, and an unrevealed one is not there at all. Nothing to declare: it follows from naming the door on the exit.
That is one verb with two jobs, which is the classic parser’s own shape: the same word boards a vehicle (see
). The door wins where an item is somehow both — a door is referenced by an exit rather than placed in a room, so boarding one by name was never possible anyway — and a
rule on the item pre-empts either.
